title: Opening of document on p.2: This report on Seychelles was prepared ...
summary: This section is mainly a list of documents included in the released package, comprising a press release announcing the Executive Board's completion of the third reviews under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility with a US$12.1 Million disbursement for Seychelles, the staff report completed on November 19, 2024, following discussions ending October 1, 2024, a staff supplement, and an Executive Director statement.

title: Press Release
summary: The IMF completed the third reviews under Seychelles’ Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility. Program performance remains good. Real GDP growth is projected at 4.3 percent in 2025, and average annual inflation is expected to reach 2.3 percent in 2025. IMF staff assess that macroeconomic stability has been maintained despite moderating growth in 2024. Staff recommend that authorities remain vigilant to inflationary pressures and adjust monetary policy if needed. Downside risks include tourism shocks, rising commodity prices, and climate change.

title: Executive Summary
summary: Real GDP growth is projected at 3 percent in 2024 compared to an earlier projection of 3.7 percent, and 4.3 percent in 2025. Year-on-year inflation is expected to hit 2.5 percent by end-2024. Downside risks include commodity price rebounds, climate change, and dampening global tourism demand. Considering the authorities' strong program implementation and policy commitments going forward, staff recommend completion of the third reviews of the EFF and RSF.

title: Context And Recent Developments
summary: Projected real GDP growth for 2024 has been revised down to 3.0 percent due to softening tourism. Year-on-year inflation is projected to reach 2.5 percent by December 2024. Staff assess that the monetary policy stance appears accommodative, though monetary transmission remains weak. The external current account deficit is expected to widen to 10.7 percent of GDP in 2024. Meanwhile, capex plans may still be under-executed, and public and publicly guaranteed debt is projected to rise to 61.5 percent of GDP by end-2024.

title: Outlook And Risks
summary: IMF staff view the outlook as broadly stable. Real GDP growth is projected to rise to 4.3 percent in 2025 and stabilize at around 3.5 percent in the medium term. Average annual inflation is projected to stabilize at around 3 percent over the medium term. The current account deficit is expected to average about 9 percent of GDP over the medium term, while reserve coverage reaches around 3.8 months of imports over the medium term. Staff highlight external downside risks.

title: Program Performance
summary: IMF staff assesses that EFF program implementation has generally been good, with all end-June 2024 quantitative targets met and net international reserves accumulation 5.6 percent above the program target. Structural reforms are moving forward despite several delays. Under the RSF, some measures proved more complex than authorities and IMF staff originally thought, prompting proposed modifications for five of the remaining nine reform measures. Dropping negative climate tagging appears infeasible before the program ends, while overall reform ambition remains high.

title: Policy Discussions
summary: IMF staff assess the FY2025 fiscal stance as appropriately tight to achieve public debt of 50 percent of GDP or less by 2030, with public debt assessed as sustainable with high probability. A primary fiscal surplus of 1.1 percent in 2024 and 1.1 percent of GDP in FY2025 is expected. Staff consider the broadly neutral monetary policy stance appropriate, recommending a data-dependent approach. Staff highlight risks from tourism competition, bank interest rate spreads, and central bank balance sheet vulnerabilities.

title: Program Modalities
summary: IMF staff assess risks to the EFF and RSF as moderate, the EFF as fully financed, and Seychelles' capacity to repay the Fund as adequate but subject to risks. Upon approval of the third reviews, SDR 6.107 million under the EFF and SDR 3.123 million under the RSF will be used for budget support. Six new structural benchmarks and revised targets are proposed for 2025, including raising June 2025 net international reserves to $628.8 million. Fund exposure will remain high for an extended period.

title: Staff Appraisal
summary: IMF staff assesses economic activity as moderating and external vulnerabilities elevated. Fiscal policies for 2024 and 2025 are viewed as appropriate, with the FY2024 primary surplus projected at 1.1 percent of GDP. Staff recommends a careful, data-driven monetary policy and assesses financial sector risks as low. Finally, staff supports the authorities' request for completion of the third reviews under the EFF and RSF, assessing implementation risks as manageable.

title: Annex I. Risk Assessment Matrix
summary: This section is mainly a table presenting the Risk Assessment Matrix, which reflects IMF staff views on conjunctural risks that may materialize over a horizon between 12 to 18 months, with staff assessments assigning subjective probabilities below 10 percent, between 10 and 30 percent, and between 30 and 50 percent, alongside structural risks and recommended policy responses.

title: Annex II. Interest Rate Spread in Seychelles
summary: IMF staff assesses that persistently high interest rate spreads, hovering around 9 percentage points since September 2008, hamper growth and monetary policy effectiveness. Given market diseconomies of scale, staff views new bank entry as ineffective, recommending instead nonbank financing, digital banking, and creditor legal reforms. Crucially, staff cautions that narrowing spreads without reducing costs poses risks to bank profitability and could cause underpricing of credit risk amid elevated nonperforming loans.

title: Annex III. Financial Sector Reform Measures Under the 2024-26
summary: This section is mainly a table detailing proposed changes to Seychelles' financial sector reform measures, reflecting IMF staff's assessment that original measures approved in July 2023 critically overestimated Central Bank of Seychelles capacity, necessitating the redesign and delayed implementation of measures for March 2025 and September 2025 to address technical constraints, Fund staff knowledge gaps, and climate-related data gaps.

title: Appendix I. Letter of Intent
summary: Seychelles projects 2024 real GDP growth at 3.02 percent, lowered from 3.69 percent, while the public and publicly guaranteed debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to reach 61.5 percent by end-2024. All quantitative targets were met. IMF staff assessed that the current program performance-based budgeting approach is complex with insufficient strategic focus, recommending that medium-term budget framework preparation be aligned with good practice. The authorities request completing the third program review.

title: Opening of document on p.93: This supplement provides additional information to ...
summary: This section is mainly a table outlining program structural benchmarks and reform measures. The IMF staff view is that staff projections, recommendations, and the thrust of the staff appraisal remain unchanged. Additionally, on November 27, 2024, Cabinet approved the Seychelles Climate Finance Resource Mobilization Strategy 2025 - 2030 under RM5, and approved the draft Bank Recovery and Resolution Act on October 16, 2024.

title: Statement by Mr. Seong-Wook Kim, Executive Director for Seychelles
summary: The authorities report growth forecasts were revised to 3.0 percent for 2024 and 4.1 percent for 2025, with annual inflation forecasted to be 0.5 percent in 2024. The primary surplus in 2024 is projected to be 1.1 percent of GDP, anchored by a debt target of around 50 percent of GDP by 2029. Recent Fund assistance highlighted the need for enhanced linkages between the budget and the National Development Strategy. Commodity price shocks and tourism underperformance remain key risks.
